introduction.en: A linked list is a dynamic data structure where elements (nodes) are connected through pointers. Unlike arrays, memory is not contiguous — each node stores data and the address of the next node.
introduction.hi: Linked list ek dynamic data structure hai jisme elements (nodes) pointers se connected hote hain. Arrays se alag, memory contiguous nahi hoti — har node apna data aur agle node ka address store karta hai.

realLifeAnalogy.en: Think of a train — each coach (node) is connected to the next one. You can add or remove coaches easily without disturbing the others!
realLifeAnalogy.hi: Train socho — har dabba (node) agle se connected hai. Aasani se dabbe jod ya hata sakte ho bina dusron ko disturb kiye!

content.en:
A linked list is a sequence of nodes where each node contains data and a pointer to the next node. The first node is called the **head** and the last node points to NULL.

**Key Properties:**
- Dynamic size — grows/shrinks at runtime
- No random access — must traverse from head
- Efficient insertion/deletion at head: O(1)
- Extra memory for pointers
content.hi:
Linked list nodes ka ek sequence hai jisme har node mein data aur agle node ka pointer hota hai. Pehla node **head** kehlaata hai aur aakhri node NULL point karta hai.

**Important Baatein:**
- Dynamic size — runtime pe grow/shrink hoti hai
- Random access nahi — head se traverse karna padta hai
- Head pe insert/delete efficient: O(1)
- Pointers ke liye extra memory chahiye

codeExamples.python:
class Node:
    def __init__(self, val):
        self.data = val
        self.next = None

head = Node(10)
head.next = Node(20)
head.next.next = Node(30)

curr = head
while curr:
    print(curr.data, end=' ')
    curr = curr.next

keyPoints.en: Head is the entry point of a linked list
keyPoints.hi: Head linked list ka entry point hota hai

keyPoints.en: Last node's next pointer is NULL
keyPoints.hi: Aakhri node ka next pointer NULL hota hai

keyPoints.en: No index-based access — must traverse sequentially
keyPoints.hi: Index-based access nahi hoti — sequentially traverse karna padta hai

content.en:
**1. Singly Linked List** — Each node points to the next node only.
**2. Doubly Linked List** — Each node has pointers to both next and previous nodes.
**3. Circular Linked List** — Last node points back to the first node.

Doubly linked lists allow backward traversal but use extra memory. Circular lists are used in round-robin scheduling.
content.hi:
**1. Singly Linked List** — Har node sirf agle node ko point karta hai.
**2. Doubly Linked List** — Har node ke paas next aur previous dono ke pointers hote hain.
**3. Circular Linked List** — Aakhri node pehle node ko point karta hai.

Doubly linked list mein backward traversal possible hai par extra memory lagti hai. Circular list round-robin scheduling mein use hoti hai.

keyPoints.en: Singly LL: less memory, forward traversal only
keyPoints.hi: Singly LL: kam memory, sirf aage traverse ho sakta hai

keyPoints.en: Doubly LL: more memory, bidirectional traversal
keyPoints.hi: Doubly LL: zyada memory, dono directions mein traverse

keyPoints.en: Circular LL: no NULL end, useful for round-robin
keyPoints.hi: Circular LL: koi NULL end nahi, round-robin ke liye useful

content.en:
**Insert at Head:** Create new node, point it to current head, update head — O(1)
**Insert at Tail:** Traverse to last node, link new node — O(n)
**Delete by Value:** Find node before target, update its next pointer — O(n)
**Reverse:** Change all next pointers to point backwards — O(n)
content.hi:
**Head pe Insert:** Naya node banao, use current head pe point karo, head update karo — O(1)
**Tail pe Insert:** Last node tak traverse karo, naya node link karo — O(n)
**Value se Delete:** Target ke pehle node dhundho, uska next pointer update karo — O(n)
**Reverse:** Saare next pointers ko peeche ki taraf point karo — O(n)

keyPoints.en: Inserting at head is O(1), at tail is O(n)
keyPoints.hi: Head pe insert O(1) hai, tail pe O(n)

keyPoints.en: Reversing a linked list uses three pointers: prev, curr, next
keyPoints.hi: Linked list reverse karne ke liye teen pointers use hote hain: prev, curr, next

keyPoints.en: Always update pointers carefully to avoid losing nodes
keyPoints.hi: Pointers carefully update karo warna nodes lost ho jaate hain

content.en:
The fast and slow pointer technique (also called Floyd's Tortoise and Hare) uses two pointers moving at different speeds to detect cycles, find the middle, or solve other problems.

**Applications:**
- Detect cycle in a linked list
- Find middle of linked list
- Find starting point of cycle
- Detect palindrome in linked list
content.hi:
Fast aur slow pointer technique (Floyd's Tortoise and Hare) mein do pointers alag alag speed se move karte hain. Isse cycles detect karte hain, middle dhundhte hain, ya aur bhi problems solve karte hain.

**Applications:**
- Linked list mein cycle detect karna
- Linked list ka middle dhundhna
- Cycle ka starting point dhundhna
- Linked list palindrome check karna

keyPoints.en: Slow pointer moves 1 step, fast pointer moves 2 steps
keyPoints.hi: Slow pointer 1 step chalta hai, fast pointer 2 steps

keyPoints.en: If they meet, cycle exists; if fast reaches NULL, no cycle
keyPoints.hi: Agar mile, cycle hai; agar fast NULL pe pahunche, cycle nahi hai

keyPoints.en: Finding middle: when fast reaches end, slow is at middle
keyPoints.hi: Middle dhundhna: jab fast end pe pahunche, slow middle pe hoga
